title: Elph auth store
description: CONFIG_DIR/auth.json. Logical document is { $schema?, provider?, mcp? }. On disk, secret strings are AES-256-GCM with an enc: prefix; env:VAR references stay plaintext. Legacy providers (plural) is accepted on load. A v2 sealed envelope { v, alg, nonce, ciphertext } is still readable but no longer written. Mode 0600 on Unix. Do not commit or attach this file.

provider.description: Map of provider id (kebab-case) → API key or env:VAR. Secrets are stored as enc:… after save.

providers.description: Legacy alias for provider. Normalized to provider on load.

mcp.description: Map of MCP server name → OAuth credentials. On disk the value is usually enc:… (ciphertext of the StoredCredentials JSON). After decrypt it is an object.

v.description: Legacy sealed-envelope version. Present only on old whole-file ciphertext stores.

nonce.description: Legacy sealed-envelope nonce (URL-safe base64, no pad).

ciphertext.description: Legacy sealed-envelope ciphertext+tag (URL-safe base64, no pad).

secretOrRef.description: enc:<base64url> (field ciphertext), env:VAR_NAME (plaintext reference), or a legacy plaintext API key (re-encrypted on next save).

mcpEntry.description: Encrypted string on disk, or a decrypted StoredCredentials object (rmcp).

tokenResponse.description: OAuth token response (access_token, refresh_token, expires_in, token_type, scope, …).
